summary: Ghosted fragments and duplicated tail segments after load-balancer failover during SSE session
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-lived Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming sessions show 1) duplicated trailing token fragments after an internal load-balancer (LB) failover, and 2) 'ghost' event fragments that arrive out-of-order or without corresponding end markers. Impact: downstream application sees duplicated partial final choices and intermittent state-machine errors when stitching choices, causing incorrect UI display and occasional instruction duplication. Environment: prod-us-east, behind our regional L7 LB, customer uses persistent SSE with client-side reconnect logic (exponential backoff + resume token). Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a long streaming session (>60s) against /v1/stream with redwood-v1.3 pinned. 2) Induce a rolling restart on one of the regional edge proxies or trigger an LB failover (simulated by removing healthy instances). 3) Allow client reconnect to resume using last-offset resume token. Observed behavior: on reconnect, client sometimes receives duplicate tail fragments (e.g. last 8-12 tokens repeated) and intermittent short 'meta fragments' that contain no content but a resume-id header; occasionally a fragment arrives after an 'end' event, producing a ghosted sentence. Expected behavior: resume should continue from the last delivered token and not produce duplicates or out-of-order fragments. Logs attached and relevant traces referenced below.
reproduction_steps: Start SSE stream to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream with model=redwood-v1.3 and stream_timeout=180s
Generate prompt expected to produce ~40s of streaming tokens (long generation)
While streaming, remove one backend from the prod-us-east L7 pool to force LB failover (or restart edge-proxy)
Observe client logs and reconstructed output after the client reconnects using resume token

comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-13): Customer reported duplicated final phrases and occasional orphan fragments after their LB did maintenance. They attached client logs and a short video showing UI duplication.

Marco Ruiz (2026-03-13): Acknowledged, triaging. Tentative hypothesis: LB failover + proxy connection close causing partial chunk re-delivery due to proxy replays or race in resume handling. Assigning to SRE and streaming-runtime owners.

SRE (Lina Chen) (2026-03-13): Confirmed failover event in prod-us-east at 18:42. Edge proxy restarted and health checks triggered. Observed short window of half-closed connections. Will pull tcpdump and proxy logs.

Streaming Runtime (Diego Alvarez) (2026-03-14): Found cases where session metadata race allows a buffered final fragment to be forwarded twice when resume token reconciliation occurs after a delayed end-event. Preparing a hotfix branch to add an idempotency check on fragment sequence ids.

Support (2026-03-14): Sent workaround to customer: enable 'sticky-sessions' on their LB or switch their client to wait 150ms after re-establish before resuming to reduce race. Customer applied sticky-sessions and reported initial reduction in duplicates; still seeing rare ghosts.
Marco Ruiz (2026-03-14): Coordinating deploy of streaming-runtime patch. Rolling canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 with additional logging toggles for fragment sequence ids.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge LB failover causes half-closed TCP connections; proxy attempts to replay buffered chunks to new backend resulting in duplicate fragments.
Hypothesis 2: Resume path in streaming-proxy does not fully reconcile last-ack offset under concurrent end-event delivery, causing a small window where the same fragment can be emitted twice.

Evidence: trace correlation shows identical fragment id and identical token checksum sent twice separated by ~120ms; client-side resume token matches server resume position but server emitted fragment again after end-event.
Mitigation tested: instruct customer to enable LB stickiness -> duplicates decreased. Also tested client-side 150ms pause before resume -> duplicates decreased in simulation.

Next steps: add idempotency by tracking recent fragment sequence ids for 1s after session end + backfill patch to avoid replay, and add extra logging to trace fragment sequence ids on production canary
resolution: Mitigation applied: Customer enabled LB sticky-sessions and temporarily reduced duplicate rate. Streaming runtime hotfix in PR (see related_github_prs) adds fragment-seq idempotency and tighter resume reconciliation; canary build scheduled 2026-03-15. Final resolution pending canary validation and full rollout.
